source_text: Μηδαμῶς γὰρ πλέον τι ὠφελουμένου τοῦ γινώσκοντος τὰ αὐτῷ συμβησόμενα παρὰ τὸν βίον καταθύμια· θῶμεν γὰρ τοῦτο· ὅμως δὲ καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων περιεργίᾳ ἐπιτεχνᾶται, ὡς καὶ τὰ μετὰ θάνατόν τινος ἑκάστου ἐσόμενα, πολυπραγμονεῖν τε καὶ δοκεῖν εἰδέναι. Μνήμη δὲ ἀγαθὴ ψυχῇ προσηνεστέρα, ἤπερ σώματι ἔλαιον· καὶ βίου ἔξοδος, ἀμείνων γενέσεως· καὶ αἱρετώτερον πενθεῖν, ἢ κωμάζειν, καὶ τὸ παρεῖναι τοῖς λυπουμένοις, ἢ τοῖς μεθυσκομένοις. Ἔστι γὰρ οὕτω, λαβόντα τινὰ τοῦ βίου τέλος μὴ εὐλαβηθῆναι περὶ τῶν ἀμφ᾽ αὐτόν. Γέλωτος δὲ θυμὸς ἔμφρων προτιμότερος· αὐστηρᾷ γὰρ διαθέσει προσώπου, κατορθοῦται ψυχή. Αἱ μὲν τοίνυν τῶν σοφῶν ψυχαὶ, σκυθρωπάζουσι καὶ συστέλλονται, αἱ δὲ τῶν ἀφρόνων ἐπαιρόμεναι διαχέονται. Πολὺ δέ ἐστιν εὐκταιότερον ἐπίπληξιν σοφοῦ ἑνὸς δέξασθαι, ἢ ὅλου χοροῦ ἀνθρώπων φαύλων καὶ δυστήνων ᾀδόντων γενέσθαι ἀκροατήν. Τῶν γὰρ ἀφρόνων ἀνθρώπων ὁ γέλως, ἀκανθῶν πολλῶν λάβρῳ πυρὶ καιομένων ἤχῳ προσέοικεν. Ἄθλιον δὲ καὶ τοῦτο, κακόν γε μὴν μέγιστον ἡ συκοφαντία· αὕτη γὰρ σοφῶν ἐπιβουλεύει ψυχαῖς, καὶ ἐπιχειρεῖ διαφθείρειν τὴν γενναίαν ἔνστασιν τῶν ἀγαθῶν. Λόγων δὲ οὐκ ἀρχόμενον, ἀλλὰ παυόμενον ἐπαινεῖν προσήκει, καὶ τὸ μέτριον ἦθος ἀποδέχεσθαι, καὶ μὴ τὸ μετεωριζόμενον καὶ τετυφωμένον. Πάνυ δὲ χρὴ θυμοῦ φείδεσθαι, καὶ μὴ εἰς ὀργὴν προχείρως καταφέρεσθαι, ᾗτινι ἄφρονες δουλεύουσιν.
thought_title: Mourning and rebuke are better than laughter and songs
orientation: Solomon's teaching continues with a chain of what is better in human life.
pass_a_gloss: For in no way is the one who knows the things that will happen to him during his life benefited anything more than by things pleasing to his heart; for let us posit this; yet also by the meddlesomeness of men it is contrived both to busy themselves about the things that will be after the death of each one and to seem to know. And a good remembrance is more pleasing to soul than oil to body; and departure from life is better than birth; and to mourn is more to be chosen than to revel, and to be present with those who grieve than with those who are drunk. For it is so that one who has received the end of life is not to fear concerning those around him. And thoughtful anger is more to be preferred than laughter; for by stern disposition of face soul is made straight. Therefore the souls of the wise are gloomy and are drawn together, but those of the foolish, being lifted up, are poured apart. And it is much more to be prayed for to receive rebuke of one wise man than to become hearer of a whole chorus of worthless and miserable men singing. For the laughter of foolish men is like the sound of many thorns being burned with violent fire. And this too is wretched, and slander is the greatest evil; for this plots against souls of wise men, and attempts to corrupt the noble firm standing of good things. And it is fitting to praise of words not the beginning but the ceasing, and to accept the moderate character and not the one lifted high and puffed up. And it is very necessary to spare anger and not to be carried down readily into wrath, to which foolish men are enslaved.

choices.why: adverbial neuter plural for what suits desire, parallel to benefit in life, not sacrifice
θυμὸς is anger or passion and ἔμφρων qualifies it as sensible, keeping the contrast with laughter

choices.english: noble firm standing of good things
choices.why: ἔνστασις is standing firm and γενναίαν is noble, describing steadfastness attacked by slander
participle contrasts with beginning and means stopping point, matching end better than beginning

pass_b_english: Knowing in advance the things pleasing to his heart that will meet him in life does the knower no good at all. Grant that for the sake of argument. Yet human meddling still contrives a further curiosity: to pry into what will come to each person after death and to claim to know it.

A good name delights the soul more than oil delights the body, and the end of life is better than its beginning (Ecclesiastes 7:1). It is better to mourn than to revel, and better to sit with those who grieve than with those who are drunk (Ecclesiastes 7:2). In this way, one who has reached the end of life has no anxiety about those around him. Thoughtful anger is better than laughter, for a stern face sets the soul straight (Ecclesiastes 7:3). The souls of the wise grow somber and restrained, while the souls of fools swell up and dissolve.

It is far more desirable to accept a rebuke from one wise man than to listen to a whole chorus of worthless and wretched men singing (Ecclesiastes 7:5). For the laughter of fools sounds like many thorns crackling in a fierce fire (Ecclesiastes 7:6). Slander is miserable as well, and indeed the greatest evil, for it plots against the souls of the wise and tries to corrupt the noble firm standing of good things (Ecclesiastes 7:7). One should praise the ceasing of words, not their beginning, and approve a measured temper, not one that is lofty and puffed up (Ecclesiastes 7:8). Above all, spare anger and do not rush headlong into rage, to which fools are enslaved (Ecclesiastes 7:9).

last_rejected.quote: the noble firm standing of good things
last_rejected.why: Parallel to σοφῶν, τῶν ἀγαθῶν are good people; slander attacks their steadfastness, not abstract goods.
last_rejected.fix: tries to corrupt the noble steadfastness of the good.
last_rejected.ruling: τῶν ἀγαθῶν is ambiguous (neuter or masculine); 'good things' is within range, though parallel with σοφῶν suggests people. ἔνστασις rendering fine. Preference, not clear meaning change.
